record.paper_title: Dense ideals in topological algebras: some results and open problems
record.original_question: If A is an F-algebra that is also a division algebra, must A be isomorphic to the complex field C?

evidence.quote: – The class F of all F-algebras, i.e. completely metrisable topological algebras.
Problem 2. Is it true that a division algebra of type F is isomorphic to C ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define an F-algebra to be a complex associative algebra A equipped with a topology making A a completely metrisable topological vector space and such that the multiplication A × A → A is jointly continuous (equivalently, an associative complex algebra whose underlying topological vector space is a complete metrisable t.v.s., with separately or jointly continuous multiplication in the standard sense used for completely metrisable topological algebras). Assume A has a unit element. Recall that A is called a division algebra if every nonzero element of A has a (two-sided) multiplicative inverse in A.

Question: Must every F-algebra that is also a division algebra be isomorphic, as a complex algebra, to the field ℂ of complex numbers?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the Gelfand–Mazur theorem extends to F-algebras (i.e., whether every completely metrisable topological division algebra over ℂ is isomorphic to ℂ) is a long-standing open problem. Partial results exist: Turpin–Waelbroeck showed it holds under the additional assumption of continuity of inversion together with a continuous p-homogeneous seminorm, but the general case remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: F-Algebra - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
status_evidence.snippet: One of the important still open questions is the problem whether the Gelfand–Mazur theorem is valid for algebras of type F, i.e. whether every division algebra in this class is trivial (topologically isomorphic to C ...).
status_evidence.claim: The Gelfand–Mazur problem for F-algebras is described as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Commutative Banach Algebras: Shilov's idempotent theorem (thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Turpin and Waelbroeck: every complex topological division algebra with continuous inverse and a continuous p-homogeneous seminorm is topologically isomorphic to C.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results (under extra assumptions) are known.
